Identity: codex-storymodel-l1b-audit. One acceptance law to add to the new semantic-zoom bead; no new bead and no source edit from me.

ZOOM-4 — CONTINUOUS GESTURE, DISCRETE SEMANTICS, LAST INTENT WINS. ZoomLevel is a finite typed state, so a continuous wheel/pinch/range gesture needs a deterministic StoryAtlas-side transition policy: explicit thresholds plus hysteresis, independent of frame rate. Otherwise tiny input noise can alternate Story/Hidden and Episode/Sentences, repeatedly recompiling and making marks flicker while every individual compilation remains lawful. Camera scale may interpolate visually between committed states, but the displayed semantic state and receipt must always name one exact ZoomLevel.

The novel-scale version becomes an async correctness law. If compile request n targets Episode/Sentences and request n+1 immediately returns to Story/Hidden, a delayed result n must not overwrite n+1. Bind every response to the input ViewChoice/configuration checksum (or a monotonically increasing local intent revision) and discard stale completions before DOM replacement. Selection, Address, horizon and Codex focus remain the state carried through both requests; only a result matching the current intent may become visible.

Capacity scenario for bd-01M16KD7WBWKTQC6CENE9V67Q0: inject a controllable compiler where request n resolves after n+1; cross a semantic threshold and reverse; assert the final DOM receipts/mark-id set/placement equal n+1, not whichever future completed last. Separately jitter the gesture on both sides of one threshold and assert hysteresis prevents representation oscillation. This is a StoryAtlas interaction/runtime law, not a new storymodel4s scale or a renderer inference.
